messages:
sre-oncall: :rotating_light: Seeing sustained p99 latency spikes on Dedicated pool `eu-west-2-ded-42` since 11:00 UTC, customer SLA at risk. Throughput for the pool dropped ~35%.
cheng: Noted. Any immediate noisy-tenant suspects? recent placement/quotas changed?
sre-oncall: Ops deck shows a quota bump rollout yesterday for small-commit customers; placement logs show many tiny slices packed on G4dn nodes. Might be densification gone wrong.
junaid: I pulled a perf profile from 11:05-11:20 with `nsys` and our internal tracer. Key lines: 
```
GPU kernels: 70% fast-kernel, 30% fallback-slow-kernel
Avg batch size: 2.1 (target 8)
KV cache hit-rate: 54% (baseline 87%)
Scheduler queue length: spikes to 120
```
leah: KV cache hit-rate drop is worrying — looks like aggressive eviction. Any recent config changes to cache sizing or TTL?
sre-oncall: Cache TTL unchanged, but node packing increased number of tenants per GPU, so working set per tenant exceeded local cache. Evictions jumped.
eva: The fallback-slow-kernel events line up with sequence-length variance: several requests hit >1024 tokens, and our kernel selection fallback threshold was lowered last week by the runtime team.
cheng: Right — the runtime change to prefer quantized fast kernels added a guard that falls back on dynamic-length mismatch. Under densified packing, variance increases because small tenants get batched with a long tail and kernel selector degenerates. That's causing both slow kernels and lower batching efficiency.
matt: Also seeing head-of-line blocking from batching heuristics: continuous-batcher waits 20ms window then flushes, but with small batch sizes it triggers more frequent tiny batches.
opsbot: deploy-bot: Reverted commit `runtime/selector:lower-fallback-threshold` at 11:40 UTC in staging. Rollout to prod pending.
sre-oncall: Immediate mitigation plan?
junaid: Short-term: 1) Isolate top offending tenant(s) by moving them to separate nodes (reduce noisy neighbor). 2) Raise KV cache allocation on packed nodes to restore hit-rate. 3) Temporarily widen batching window to 40ms for affected pool to increase avg batch size.
leah: I'm starting the isolation move for tenant ids t-9843 and t-6612 now (will throttle placement). ETA ~7min.
eva: I'll prepare a runtime patch to revert the fallback threshold change and add a guard that prevents mixing very long sequences into the same batch. Quick PR ready for review.
matt: Can we also add an autoscaler rule that prevents >N small-tenant sockets per GPU? That would avoid pathological densification.
cheng: Agree. Longer-term: change kernel selector to be aware of sequence-length distribution and to prefer per-tenant mini-batches for tail sequences, plus smarter KV cache allocation per tenant. Add profiler counters for kernel-fallback and kv-eviction to alert earlier.
opsbot: infra-bot: Current node utilization on eu-west-2-ded-42: GPU util 92%, Mem 88%, tenant-slices 47. Moving tenants now.
sre-oncall: Isolation move complete, affected tenant moved to dedicated nodes. p99 back down to baseline after ~6m. Throughput recovered ~28%. SLA breach avoided for now.
cheng: We should still triage root cause offline: sequence-length telemetry + placement policy + quota rollout interplay. I'll open an incident follow-up issue with attached traces and the `nsys` sample.
leah: Adding perf regression label and linking the KV-cache dashboard.
matt: Also add a playbook step: when p99 spike + low avg batch size => consider isolation + widen batch window before reverting runtime.
sre-oncall: Thanks everyone. Postmortem incoming. :thumbsup:
